subclasses.name: Ancestral Guardian
description: Some barbarians hail from cultures that revere their ancestors. These tribes teach that the warriors of the past linger in the world as mighty spirits, who can guide and protect the living. When barbarians who follow this path rage, they channel these protective spirits, using them to guard their allies and enemies.

features.name: Ancestral Protectors
description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, spectral warriors appear when you enter your rage. While you're raging, the first creature you hit with an attack on your turn has disadvantage on any attack target that isn't you or the warrior. Additionally, if the target tries to make an attack while within 5 feet of you, it must first make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target must choose a different target or the attack fails. On a successful save, the target can make its attack as normal. This effect lasts until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Spirit Shield
description: Beginning at 6th level, the guardian spirits that aid you can provide protection to those you defend. If a creature you can see takes damage while within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6. You can reduce the damage by an additional 1d6 at 10th level (3d6) and at 14th level (4d6).

features.name: Consult the Spirits
description: At 10th level, you cast the augury or clairvoyance spell, without requiring a spell slot or material components, and you regain the ability to cast it this way when you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

features.name: Vengeful Ancestors
description: At 14th level, your ancestral spirits can hinder your foes even more. When you use your Spirit Shield to reduce the damage of an attack, the attacker takes an amount of force damage equal to the damage your Spirit Shield prevents.

subclasses.name: Berserker
description: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end--that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammeled fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker's rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.

features.name: Frenzy
description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).

features.name: Mindless Rage
description: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
description:
Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
 If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

features.name: Retaliation
description: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Storm Herald
description: All barbarians harbor a fury within. Their rage grants them superior strength, durability, and speed. Barbarians who follow the Path of the Storm Herald learn to transform that rage into a mantle of primal magic, which swirls around them. When in a fury, a barbarian of this path can protect their allies and harm their foes with the power of the elements.

features.name: Storm Aura
description:
Starting at 3rd level, you emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover. Your aura has a different effect depending on the environment you choose when you enter your rage: Desert, Sea, or Tundra.

Desert: When this effect is activated, all other creatures of your choice in your aura take 2 fire damage each. The damage increases to 3 at 5th level, 4 at 10th level, 5 at 15th level, and 6 at 20th level.

Sea: When this effect is activated, you can choose one other creature you can see in your aura. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. The target takes 1d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 2d6 at 10th level, 3d6 at 15th level, and 4d6 at 20th level.

Tundra: When this effect is activated, each creature of your choice in your aura gains 2 temporary hit points, which last until your rage ends. The temporary hit points increase to 3 at 5th level, 4 at 10th level, 5 at 15th level, and 6 at 20th level.

features.name: Storm Soul
description:
At 6th level, the storm grants you benefits even when your rage isn't active. You gain resistance to the damage type associated with your chosen environment: fire (Desert), lightning (Sea), or cold (Tundra).

In addition, as an action, you can create a bolt of lightning or a wave of freezing cold. If you chose Desert, you can cast the produce flame cantrip, requiring no material components. If you chose Sea, you can cast the create or destroy water spell, requiring no material components. If you chose Tundra, you can cast the fog cloud spell, requiring no material components. You can cast these spells without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them this way when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Shielding Storm
description: At 10th level, the storm you channel grows powerful enough to resist magical effects. Each creature of your choice that you can see in your aura has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

features.name: Raging Storm
description:
At 14th level, the storm you channel responds to your fury. When you use your Storm Aura, you can choose one additional effect based on your chosen environment:

Desert: When a creature starts its turn in your aura, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn.

Sea: When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to the attacker equal to your rage damage bonus.

Tundra: When a creature starts its turn in your aura, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

subclasses.name: Totem Warrior
description: The Path of the Totem Warrior is a spiritual journey, as the barbarian accepts a spirit animal as guide, protector, and inspiration. In battle, your totem spirit fills you with supernatural might, adding magical fuel to your barbarian rage.
Most barbarian tribes consider a totem animal to be kin to the members of the tribe. It is rare for an individual to have more than one totem animal spirit in a lifetime, though exceptions exist.

features.name: Spirit Seeker
description: Yours is a path that seeks attunement with the natural world, granting you a kinship with beasts. At 3rd level when you adopt this path, you gain the ability to cast the beast sense and speak with animals spells, but only as rituals.

features.name: Totem Spirit
description: At 3rd level, when you adopt this path, you choose a totem spirit and gain a totem feature. You must make or acquire a physical totem object — an amulet or similar adornment — that incorporates fur or feathers, claws, teeth, or bones of the animal you choose. At your option, you also gain minor physical attributes from your totem animal. Your choices and the associated benefits are:
Bear. While raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic damage.
Eagle. While raging, other creatures have disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you, and you can use the Dash action as a bonus action on your turn.
Wolf. While raging, your friends have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you that is hostile to you.

features.name: Aspect of the Beast
description: At 6th level, you gain a magical benefit based on the totem animal you choose. You can choose the same animal you chose at 3rd level or a different one.
Bear. You gain the might of a bear. Your carrying capacity (including load, lift, and push) is doubled, and you have advantage on Strength checks made to push, pull, lift, or break objects.

Eagle. You gain the eyesight of an eagle. You can see up to 1 mile away with no difficulty, able to discern even fine details as though looking at something no more than 100 feet away from you. Additionally, dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks.
Wolf. You gain the hunting sensibilities of a wolf. You can track other creatures while traveling at a brisk pace, and you can move stealthily while traveling at a normal pace.

features.name: Spirit Walker
description: At 10th level, you can cast the commune with nature spell, but only as a ritual. When you do so, a spiritual version of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast makes itself known to you and appears somewhere on the land you are in.

features.name: Totemic Attunement
description: At 14th level, you gain a magical benefit based on a totem animal you choose. You can choose the same animal you chose at 3rd level or a different one.

Bear. While raging, any creature within 5 feet of you that's hostile to you has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you or another character with this feature. An enemy is immune to this effect if it can't see or hear you or if it can't be frightened.
Eagle. While raging, you have a flying speed equal to your current speed. This benefit works only in short bursts; you fall if you end your turn in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft.
Wolf. While raging, you can use a bonus action on your turn to knock a Large or smaller creature prone when you hit it with a melee weapon attack.

subclasses.name: Zealot
description: Some deities inspire their followers to channel unrelenting ferocity. These barbarians are zealots—warriors who channel their rage into powerful displays of divine might.

features.name: Divine Fury
description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can channel divine power to fuel your attacks. If you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack while raging, you can roll one additional damage die and add it to the damage of the attack. The damage is of the same type as the attack's normal damage type. At 14th level, you roll two additional damage dice instead of one.

features.name: Warrior of the Gods
description: At 6th level, the divine power that fuels your rage allows you to shrug off fatal blows. When you would drop to 0 hit points as a result of taking damage, you can make a Charisma saving throw (DC 5 + the damage taken). On a success, you drop to 1 hit point instead. After the saving throw succeeds, you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Fanatical Focus
description: At 10th level, the divine power that fuels your rage can help you push through harm. If you fail a saving throw while raging, you can reroll it, and you must use the new roll. You can use this ability only once per rage.

features.name: Zealous Presence
description: At 14th level, you learn to channel divine power to inspire zealotry in others. As a bonus action, you unleash a battle cry infused with divine energy. Up to ten creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear you have advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: College of Glamour
description: The College of Glamour is the home of bards who mastered their craft in the vibrant realm of the Feywild or under the tutelage of someone who dwelled there. Tutored by satyrs, eladrin, and other fey creatures, these bards learn to use their magic to delight and captivate others.

features.name: Mantle of Inspiration
description: When you join the College of Glamour at 3rd level, you gain the ability to weave a song of fey magic that imbues your allies with vigor and speed. As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to grant yourself a wondrous appearance. When you do so, choose up to five creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you. Each target gains 5 temporary hit points and can use its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

features.name: Enthralling Performance
description: Starting at 6th level, you can use musical or oratorial performance to weave a song of fey magic that charms your listeners. If you perform for at least 1 minute, you can then choose a number of humanoids within 60 feet of you who watched or listened to your performance, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you. While charmed, the target idolates you and hinders anyone attempting to harm you, but it will not obey your orders. This effect ends on a target after 1 hour, if it takes damage, if you attack it, or if it witnesses you attacking its allies. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Mantle of Majesty
description: At 14th level, you gain the ability to cloak yourself in a fey majesty. As a bonus action, you cast command, requiring no spell slot or material components, and you take on an appearance of unearthly beauty (as the alter self spell, but only affecting your appearance). The spell lasts for 1 minute. During that time, you can cast command as a bonus action on each of your turns, without expending a spell slot. Any creature charmed by you automatically fails its saving throw against the command spell you cast with this feature. Once you use this bonus action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to use it again.

subclasses.name: College of Swords
description: Bards of the College of Swords are called blades, and they entertain through daring feats of weapon prowess. They perform stunts such as sword swallowing, knife throwing, and juggling. Though they use their weapons to entertain, they are highly trained and skilled warriors.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you join the College of Swords at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, scimitars, and the performer's kit.

features.name: Fighting Style
description: At 3rd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options: Dueling, Two-Weapon Fighting, or Great Weapon Fighting. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you get to choose again.

choices.name: Dueling
choices.description: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

choices.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
choices.description: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

choices.name: Great Weapon Fighting
choices.description: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

features.name: Blade Flourish
description: At 3rd level, you learn to perform impressive displays of martial prowess and speed. Whenever you take the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to use one of the following flourishes: Defensive Flourish, Slashing Flourish, or Mobile Flourish. Defensive Flourish: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to add the number you roll to your AC until the start of your next turn. Slashing Flourish: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal extra damage to the target you hit and to any other creature of your choice within 5 feet of you. Mobile Flourish: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to push the target you hit up to 15 feet away from you, plus a number of feet equal to the number you roll on the Bardic Inspiration die. The target is pushed to an unoccupied space of your choice.

features.name: Extra Attack
description: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Master Flourish
description: Starting at 14th level, whenever you use a Blade Flourish option, you can roll a d6 and use it instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.

subclasses.name: College of Whispers
description: Most bards share their tales with a wide audience. The bards of the College of Whispers, however, use their knowledge to uncover secrets and turn them against others through dread and fear.

features.name: Psychic Blades
description: When you join the College of Whispers at 3rd level, you learn to make your weapon attacks especially deadly. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage to that target. The damage increases to 3d6 at 5th level, 5d6 at 10th level, 8d6 at 15th level, and 10d6 at 20th level.

features.name: Words of Terror
description: At 6th level, you can weave words of dread to frighten a creature. If you speak to a humanoid alone for at least 1 minute, you can then attempt to seed paranoia in its mind. At the end of the conversation, the target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you or another creature of your choice. The frightened condition lasts for 1 hour, until the target is attacked or damaged, or until the target witnesses its allies being attacked or damaged. If the target succeeds on the saving throw, the target doesn't suspect that you tried to frighten it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Mantle of Whispers
description: At 14th level, you gain the ability to adopt a humanoid's persona. When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can magically capture its shadow using your reaction. You retain this shadow until you use it or finish a long rest. You can use the shadow as a disguise, as the disguise self spell, but it affects only your appearance. You can also use the shadow to gain information about the creature, as the speak with dead spell, but you can only ask one question. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Lore
description: Bards of the College of Lore know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge from sources as diverse as scholarly tomes and peasant tales. Whether singing folk ballads in taverns or elaborate compositions in royal courts, these bards use their gifts to hold audiences spellbound. When the applause dies down, the audience members might find themselves questioning everything they held to be true, from their faith in the priesthood of the local temple to their loyalty to the king. The loyalty of these bards lies in the pursuit of beauty and truth, not in fealty to a monarch or following the tenets of a deity. A noble who keeps such a bard as a herald or advisor knows that the bard would rather be honest than politic. The college's members gather in libraries and sometimes in actual colleges, complete with classrooms and dormitories, to share their lore with one another. They also meet at festivals or affairs of state, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words
description:
Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.
When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll.
You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.

features.name: Additional Magical Secrets
description: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.

choices.name: spell1
choices.description: Choose one spell from any class

choices.name: spell2
choices.description: Choose another spell from any class

features.name: Peerless Skill
description: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the GM tells you whether you succeed or fail.

subclasses.name: Valor
description: Bards of the College of Valor are daring skalds, telling tales of great heroes and performing deeds worthy of song. They wander the land to witness great events firsthand and see the deeds of legendary heroes.

As they travel from place to place, these bards inspire others with songs and stories of past glories, stirring their audiences to greatness and spurring them to action. The college's members gather to share their lore with one another and celebrate their common bond.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Combat Inspiration
description: Also at 3rd level, you learn to inspire others in combat. A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against that attack, after seeing the roll but before knowing whether it hits or misses.

features.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Battle Magic
description: At 14th level, you have mastered the art of weaving spellcasting and weapon use together. When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Forge Domain
description: The gods of the forge are patrons of artisans who work with metal, from a humble blacksmith to an elven smith who mithral. The gods of the forge teach that, with patience and hard work, even the most intractable metal can be transformed from a lump of iron into a beautiful object. Clerics of the forge domain are the divine embodiment of the power of the forge.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

features.name: Blessing of the Forge
description: At 1st level, you gain the ability to imbue magic into a weapon or armor. At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next long rest or until you die, the object becomes a magic item, granting a +1 bonus to AC (armor) or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls (weapon). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Artisan's Blessing
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to create a nonmagical item that is worth no more than 100 gp. The item must be made of metal, and you must spend 10 minutes in prayer and work to create it. The item can be a suit of armor, a weapon, a set of tools, or another object. The object appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. If you create a weapon, it is a simple or martial weapon of your choice. If you create a suit of armor, it is light, medium, or heavy armor of your choice. If you create a set of tools, they are artisan's tools of your choice.

features.name: Soul of the Forge
description: Starting at 6th level, your mastery of the forge grants you special resistances. You gain resistance to fire damage. In addition, while you are wearing heavy armor, you have a +1 bonus to AC.

features.name: Divine Strike
description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Saint of Forge and Fire
description: At 17th level, your blessed affinity with the forge gains divine benefits. You gain immunity to fire damage. In addition, while you are wearing heavy armor, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.

subclasses.name: Grave Domain
description: Gods of the grave watch over the line between life and death. To these deities, death and the afterlife are a foundational part of the multiverse. To desecrate the peace of the dead is an abomination. Deities of the grave include Kelemvor, Wee Jas, and the ancestors of many cultures.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Circle of Mortality
description: At 1st level, you gain the ability to manipulate the line between life and death. When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points to a creature at 0 hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. In addition, you learn the spare the dying cantrip, which doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. For you, it has a range of 30 feet, and you can cast it as a bonus action.

features.name: Eyes of the Grave
description: At 1st level, you gain the ability to sense the presence of the undead. As an action, you can open your awareness to magically detect undead. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any undead within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover and that isn't protected from divination magic. This sense doesn't tell you anything about the creature's capabilities or identity. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Path to the Grave
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to mark a creature close to death for destruction. As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, cursing it until the end of your next turn. The next time you or an ally of yours hits the cursed creature with an attack, the creature has vulnerability to all damage from that attack, and then the curse ends.

features.name: Sentinel at Death's Door
description: At 6th level, you gain the ability to impede death's progress. When you or a creature within 30 feet of you succeeds on a death saving throw or succeeds on a saving throw against a disease or effect that causes the poisoned condition, you can use your reaction to cancel the effect. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Divine Strike
description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage. When you reach 14th level, the extra extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Keeper of Souls
description: Starting at 17th level, you can seize a trace of vitality from a soul that has recently passed on. When a creature you can see dies within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a Charisma check (DC 10). On a success, you steal some of the creature's life force, and you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature gains temporary hit points equal to the result of the check. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Knowledge
description: The Knowledge domain represents the pursuit of knowledge and understanding of the world and the gods. Its clerics are scholars, sages, and seekers of truth, using their divine gifts to uncover secrets and illuminate the mysteries of existence.

Gods of knowledge—including Oghma, Boccob, Gilean, and Aureon—value learning and understanding above all. Some teach that knowledge is to be gathered and shared in libraries and universities, while others believe it should be kept secret and used only by the worthy.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge
description: At 1st level, you learn two languages of your choice and gain two skills of your choice.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to tap into a reservoir of knowledge. As an action, you become proficient in one skill or tool of your choice until you finish a short or long rest. You can use this feature again after a short or long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
description: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to read a creature's thoughts. You can then use your access to the creature's mind to command it, probe it, or probe its memories.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Visions of the Past
description: Starting at 17th level, you can call upon your deity to reveal visions of the past. You can receive visions of the past by spending at least 1 minute in meditation and prayer, and you can receive visions of the past of a specific object, creature, or location.

subclasses.name: Life
description: The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy--one of the fundamental forces of the universe--that sustains all life. The gods of life promote vitality and health through healing the sick and wounded, caring for those in need, and driving away the forces of death and undeath. Almost any non-evil deity can claim influence over this domain, particularly agricultural deities, sun gods, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life
description: Also starting at 1st level, your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
description:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured.
As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level.
Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.

features.name: Blessed Healer
description: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Divine Strike
description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Supreme Healing
description: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.

subclasses.name: Light
description: The Light domain represents the power of light, fire, and revelation. Its clerics are beacons of hope and clarity, using radiant energy to burn away darkness, undeath, and deception.

Gods of light—including Lathander, Pelor, Ra, and Apollo—promote the ideals of rebirth and renewal, truth, vigilance, and beauty, often using the symbol of the sun. Gods of the Light domain are often associated with fire as a symbol of purity and truth.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
description: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Warding Flare
description: At 1st level, you can interpose divine light between yourself and an enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker. An attacker can't benefit from this feature if it can't see or is immune to being blinded. You can use this number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to flood an area with radiant energy.

features.name: Improved Flare
description: Starting at 6th level, you can cast the fireball spell once per long rest.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Corona of Light
description: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to emanate a bright light. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that. Creatures of your choice in the bright light have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and on saving throws against spells that deal fire or radiant damage. You can end this effect on yourself early by using a bonus action to dismiss it.

subclasses.name: Nature
description: The Nature domain represents the power of the natural world. Its clerics are guardians of the wild, calling upon the primal forces of nature to protect the land and all its creatures.

Gods of nature—including Silvanus, Mielikki, and the Oak Father—revere the natural world and protect it from those who would do it harm. They teach that all living things are connected and that the balance of nature must be maintained.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature
description: At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Charm Animals and Plants
description: Starting at 1st level, you can use your action to charm one beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until you or your allies damage it.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to charm animals and plants. As an action, you touch a beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until you or your allies damage it.

features.name: Dampen Elements
description: Starting at 6th level, you can use your reaction to reduce damage. When you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to the creature against that instance of damage.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Master of Nature
description: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to charm beasts and plants. When you use your Channel Divinity to charm animals and plants, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 10 minutes or until you or your allies damage it.

subclasses.name: Tempest
description: The Tempest domain represents the power of storms and the sea. Its clerics are fierce warriors who call upon the fury of thunder and lightning to smite their enemies and protect the innocent.

Gods of the Tempest domain—including Talos, Umberlee, and Zeus—embrace the destructive power of nature and teach that only through conflict and struggle can strength be gained. They are often patrons of sailors and those who make their living on the sea.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Wrath of the Storm
description: Also at 1st level, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see. When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to deal 2d8 lightning damage to the attacker. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to maximize the damage of your lightning or thunder spells.

features.name: Thunderbolt Strike
description: Starting at 6th level, when you deal lightning damage to a creature, you can push it up to 10 feet away.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Stormborn
description: Starting at 17th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. Additionally, whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that deals lightning or thunder damage, you can fly up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

subclasses.name: Trickery
description: The Trickery domain represents the power of deception and illusion. Its clerics are cunning and resourceful, using their divine gifts to confuse and misdirect their enemies.

Gods of trickery—including Olidammara, the Traveler, and Loki—are patrons of thieves, scoundrels, and tricksters. They teach that one must be clever to survive in a world full of dangers and that sometimes the best way to defeat an enemy is through cunning rather than force.

features.name: Blessing of the Trickster
description: At 1st level, you can use your action to touch a willing creature to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to create an illusory duplicate of yourself. As an action, you create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 1 minute, or until you lose concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell). You can use your action to move the illusion up to 30 feet to a space you can see. The illusion is intangible and can't attack or take damage.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
description: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to become invisible. As an action, you become invisible until the end of your next turn, or until you attack or force a creature to make a saving throw.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Divine Strike
description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Improved Duplicity
description: At 17th level, you can create up to four illusory duplicates of yourself instead of one. You can use your action to move any number of them up to 30 feet, to spaces you can see.

subclasses.name: War
description: The War domain represents the power of battle and conflict. Its clerics are divine warriors who inspire their allies and strike down their foes with righteous fury.

Gods of war—including Tempus, Nike, and Tyr—embrace the glory of combat and teach that conflict can be a noble pursuit when waged for a just cause. They inspire their followers to fight with honor and courage in the face of overwhelming odds.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: War Priest
description: Also at 1st level, you can make a bonus action attack when you use the Attack action. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to add +10 to an attack roll.

features.name: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
description: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to grant resistance to an ally. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to its attack roll.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Avatar of Battle
description: At 17th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.

subclasses.name: Circle of Dreams
description: Druids who are members of the Circle of Dreams hail from regions that have strong ties to the Feywild and its dreamlike realms. The druids' guardianship of the natural world makes them natural allies of the fey.

features.name: Balm of the Summer Court
description: At 2nd level, you become imbued with the blessings of the Summer Court. You gain a pool of fey energy represented by a number of d6s equal to your druid level. As a bonus action, you can choose one creature you can see within 120 feet of you and spend a number of those dice equal to half your druid level or less. Roll the spent dice and add them together. The target regains a number of hit points equal to the total. The target also gains 1 temporary hit point per die spent. You regain all expended dice when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow
description: At 6th level, the magic of the Feywild guards your rest. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes a saving throw or an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant advantage to the roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Hidden Paths
description: Starting at 10th level, you can use the hidden paths that some fey use to traverse space in a blink of an eye. As a bonus action, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can use your action to teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Walker in Dreams
description: At 14th level, the magic of the Feywild grants you the ability to travel mentally or physically through dreamlands. When you finish a short rest, you can cast the dream spell once without expending a spell slot. In addition, you can cast the following spells without expending a spell slot or material components: scrying (self only), teleportation circle. You can cast each of these spells once, and you regain the ability to cast them this way when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Shepherd
description: Druids of the Circle of the Shepherd commune with the spirits of nature, especially the spirits of beasts and the fey, and call to them for aid. These druids recognize that all living things play a role in the natural world.

features.name: Speech of the Woods
description: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to converse with beasts and fey. You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan. In addition, beasts can understand your speech, and you gain the ability to decipher their noises and motions. Most beasts lack the capacity for language, but a beast that knows a language can understand you.

features.name: Spirit Totem
description:
Starting at 2nd level, you can call forth nature spirits to aid you and your allies. As a bonus action, you can use your Wild Shape to magically summon a nature spirit to a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The spirit is a spectral form of a bear, hawk, or unicorn, and it creates an aura in a 30-foot radius around it. The spirit is intangible and doesn't take up space. When you summon the spirit, choose which aura it creates:

Bear: The bear spirit grants you and your allies advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and you and your allies gain temporary hit points equal to your druid level.

Hawk: The hawk spirit grants you and your allies advantage on attack rolls against any creature in the aura, and you and your allies can use a reaction to make an opportunity attack against a creature that moves out of the aura.

Unicorn: The unicorn spirit grants you and your allies advantage on ability checks made to detect anything in the aura, and when you cast a healing spell with a spell slot, you and your allies regain hit points equal to your druid level.

The spirit remains for 1 minute, until you use this feature again, or until you die.

features.name: Mighty Summoner
description: Starting at 6th level, beasts and fey that you conjure are more resilient than normal. Any beast or fey that you summon or create with a spell gains the following benefits: The creature appears with more hit points than normal: 2 extra hit points per Hit Die it has. The weapon attacks of the creature count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Guardian Spirit
description: Beginning at 10th level, when a beast or fey that you summoned or created with a spell ends its turn in your Spirit Totem aura, it regains a number of hit points equal to half your druid level.

features.name: Faithful Summons
description: Starting at 14th level, the nature spirits you commune with protect you when you are the most vulnerable. When you are reduced to 0 hit points or are incapacitated against your will, you can use your reaction to conjure a nature spirit. The spirit appears within 60 feet of you and uses the spirit bear stat block, and it gains 40 temporary hit points. The spirit acts on its own initiative count. On each of its turns, it can take only the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help action. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to command the spirit, provided you are conscious. The spirit vanishes after 1 hour, when it is reduced to 0 hit points, when you use this feature again, or when you die.

subclasses.name: Land
description: The Circle of the Land is made up of mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites through a vast oral tradition. These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of communities that hold to the Old Faith and serve as advisors to the rulers of those folk. As a member of this circle, your magic is influenced by the land where you were initiated into the circle's mysterious rites.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
description: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

choices.name: cantrip
choices.description: Choose one additional druid cantrip

features.name: Natural Recovery
description:
Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level druid, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level slot or two 1st-level slots.

features.name: Circle Spells
description:
Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to circle spells connected to the land where you became a druid.
Choose that land--arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp--and consult the associated list of spells.
Once you gain access to a circle spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

choices.name: terrain
choices.description: Choose your terrain type (arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, underdark)

features.name: Land's Stride
description:
Starting at 6th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the entangle spell.

features.name: Nature's Ward
description: When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

features.name: Nature's Sanctuary
description: When you reach 14th level, creatures of the natural world sense your connection to nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours. The creature is aware of this effect before it makes its attack against you.

subclasses.name: Moon
description: Druids of the Circle of the Moon are fierce guardians of the natural order. They undergo special rituals that allow them to take on more powerful beast forms, transforming into creatures of great strength and ferocity.

These druids meet in secret places to share information and pass along warnings. They are masters of the wild, able to call upon the most powerful beasts to aid them in their sacred duty to protect nature from those who would do it harm.

features.name: Combat Wild Shape
description: At 2nd level, you can use Wild Shape as a bonus action.

features.name: Circle Forms
description: Also at 2nd level, you can transform into more powerful beasts.

features.name: Primal Strike
description: Starting at 6th level, your attacks in beast form count as magical.

features.name: Elemental Wild Shape
description: At 10th level, you can expend two uses of Wild Shape to transform into an elemental.

features.name: Thousand Forms
description: At 14th level, you can cast the alter self spell at will.

subclasses.name: Arcane Archer
description: An Arcane Archer studies a unique elven method of archery that weaves magic into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Arcane Archers are some of the most elite warriors on the multiverse, serving as special forces for armies or as scouts for adventuring parties.

features.name: Arcane Archer Lore
description: At 3rd level, you learn magical theory or some of the secrets of nature—typically related to the force of archery and the importance of focus. You learn either the prestidigitation or the druidcraft cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Arcane Shot
description: At 3rd level, you learn to unleash special magical effects with some of your shots. When you gain this feature, you learn two Arcane Shot options of your choice. Once per turn when you fire a shortbow or longbow as part of the Attack action, you can apply one of your Arcane Shot options to the arrow. You decide to use the option after seeing the roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack hits or misses. You have two uses of this feature, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Arcane Shot Options
description:
The following options are available to you when you use your Arcane Shot feature:

Banishing Arrow: You banish the target you hit to a harmless demiplane until the end of your next turn. The target disappears, incapacitated. When the effect ends, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space.

Beguiling Arrow: Your charm inflicts psychic damage and causes the target to be charmed by you.

Bursting Arrow: The arrow creates a burst of energy that damages the target and up to two other creatures within 10 feet of it.

Enfeebling Arrow: The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target deals only half damage with weapon attacks until the end of your next turn.

Grasping Arrow: Vines burst from the arrow, grasping the target and up to two other creatures within 10 feet of it.

Mind-Scrambling Arrow: The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target can't take reactions until the start of your next turn and must roll a d6 to determine its behavior.

Piercing Arrow: You make a ranged attack with the arrow as a normal ranged attack. The arrow passes through the target to another creature.

Seeking Arrow: You gain magical insight on the location of the target. You make a ranged attack with the arrow as a normal ranged attack. If the attack misses, you can use a bonus action to make a new attack against the same target.

Shadow Arrow: You weave illusion magic into your arrow, causing the target to be blinded until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Magic Arrow
description: At 7th level, you gain the ability to infuse arrows with magic. Whenever you fire a nonmagical arrow from a shortbow or longbow, you can make it magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. This magic fades from the arrow if it hasn't been used within 1 minute after you shoot it.

features.name: Curving Shot
description: At 7th level, you learn to direct an errant arrow toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a magic arrow and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

features.name: Ever-Ready Shot
description: Starting at 15th level, your magical archery is always at the ready. You regain all expended uses of your Arcane Shot feature when you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Battle Master
description: The Battle Master is a supreme warrior who uses a variety of maneuvers to control the battlefield. Drawing on extensive combat experience and tactical knowledge, the Battle Master can turn the tide of battle with well-timed strikes and clever stratagems. Those who emulate this martial archetype combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows.

Battle Masters study the art of war, learning to read their opponents and exploit their weaknesses with precision and cunning. They use superiority dice to fuel powerful maneuvers that can disarm, trip, or push their enemies, turning the tide of battle in their favor.

features.name: Combat Superiority
description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice.

Maneuvers. You learn three maneuvers of your choice. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack. You learn two additional maneuvers of your choice at 7th, 10th, and 15th level. Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one.

Superiority Dice. You have four superiority dice, which are d8s. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain all of your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest. You gain another superiority die at 7th level and one more at 15th level.

Saving Throws. Some of your maneuvers require your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows: Maneuver save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

choices.description: Choose three maneuvers from the Battle Master list.

features.name: Student of War
description: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice.

choices.description: Choose one type of artisan's tools.

features.name: Know Your Enemy
description: Starting at 7th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice: Strength score, Dexterity score, Constitution score, Armor Class, Current hit points, Total class levels, Fighter class levels.

features.name: Improved Combat Superiority (d10)
description: At 10th level, your superiority dice turn into d10s.

features.name: Relentless
description: Starting at 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain 1 superiority die.

features.name: Improved Combat Superiority (d12)
description: At 18th level, your superiority dice turn into d12s.

subclasses.name: Cavalier
description: The Cavalier is a mounted warrior who serves as a champion for a noble cause. Cavaliers are skilled in combat, both mounted and on foot, and they are known for their unwavering dedication to their oath.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

choices.name: Animal Handling
choices.description: Gain proficiency in Animal Handling skill.

choices.name: History
choices.description: Gain proficiency in History skill.

choices.name: Insight
choices.description: Gain proficiency in Insight skill.

choices.name: Performance
choices.description: Gain proficiency in Performance skill.

choices.name: Persuasion
choices.description: Gain proficiency in Persuasion skill.

choices.name: Language (choice)
choices.description: Learn one language of your choice.

features.name: Born to the Saddle
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have advantage on saving throws made to avoid falling off your mount. If you fall off your mount and land within 5 feet of it, you take no damage. Finally, mounting or dismounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed.

features.name: Unwavering Mark
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can menace your foes, foiling their attacks and punishing them for harming others. When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can mark the creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends early if you are incapacitated or die, or if someone else marks the target. While it is within 5 feet of you, a marked creature has disadvantage on any attack roll that doesn't target you. In addition, if a marked creature deals damage to anyone other than you, you can make a special melee attack against the marked creature as a bonus action on your next turn. You have advantage on the attack roll, and if it hits, your weapon deals extra damage equal to half your fighter level. Regardless of whether you use this bonus action, you can use it a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Warding Maneuver
description: At 7th level, you learn to fend off strikes directed at you, your mount, or other creatures nearby. If you or a creature you can see within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to roll 1d8 and reduce the damage by that amount + your proficiency bonus. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Hold the Line
description: Starting at 10th level, you become a master of locking down your enemies. Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you when they move 5 feet or more while within your reach. In addition, if a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.

features.name: Ferocious Charger
description: Starting at 15th level, you can run down your foes, whether you're mounted or not. If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line right before attacking a creature and you hit it with a melee weapon attack, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be knocked prone. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Vigilant Defender
description: Starting at 18th level, you respond to danger with extraordinary vigilance. In combat, you gain a special reaction that you can take once on every creature's turn, except your turn. You can't use this reaction on the same turn that you take your normal reaction.

subclasses.name: Champion
description: The archetypal Champion focuses on the development of raw physical power honed to deadly perfection. Those who model themselves on this archetype combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows.

features.name: Improved Critical
description: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
description: Starting at 7th level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus. In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
description: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

features.name: Superior Critical
description: Starting at 15th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

features.name: Survivor
description: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

subclasses.name: Echo Knight
subclasses.description: A mysterious warrior who can summon an echo of themselves from unspent potential, the Echo Knight uses their own shadow as a weapon. These fighters are rare and often misunderstood, for they walk the line between what is and what could be.

features.name: Manifest Echo
features.description: You can use a bonus action to magically manifest a translucent, gray image of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of you. This echo lasts until it is destroyed, you dismiss it, you manifest another echo, or you're incapacitated. Your echo has AC 14 + your proficiency bonus, 1 hit point, and immunity to all conditions. If it has to make a saving throw, use your save bonus. It is the same size as you, and it occupies its space. On your turn, you can mentally command the echo to move up to 30 feet in any direction (no action required). You can use it as the origin for your attacks and you can make opportunity attacks as if you were in its space.

features.name: Unleash Incarnation
features.description: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one additional melee attack from the echo's space. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Echo Avatar
features.description: As a bonus action, you can teleport, magically swapping places with your echo at a cost of 15 feet of your movement, regardless of the distance between the two of you. Immediately before you teleport, you can see through its eyes and hear through its ears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses that the echo has. During this time, you are deaf and blind with regard to your own senses.

features.name: Shadow Martyr
features.description: When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of your echo, you can use your reaction to teleport, causing the echo to teleport to the space you were in and become the target of the attack instead. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Reclaim Potential
features.description: When your echo is destroyed by taking damage, you can use your reaction to gain a number of temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Constitution modifier. If you end your turn with these temporary hit points, you lose them. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Legion of One
features.description: When you use Manifest Echo, you can create two echoes with it, and these echoes can coexist. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one additional melee attack from the space of each echo. Moreover, when you use Unleash Incarnation, you can make the additional attack from either echo's space.

subclasses.name: Eldritch Knight
description: The Eldritch Knight combines the martial prowess of a fighter with the arcane power of a wizard. Through years of study and practice, these warriors learn to cast spells while wearing armor and wielding heavy weapons.

Eldritch Knights are versatile combatants, able to adapt to any situation by combining sword and sorcery. They are often found on the front lines, using their magical abilities to protect their allies and smite their enemies.

features.name: Spellcasting
description: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells.
Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. You learn an additional wizard cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

Spell Slots. The Eldritch Knight Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your wizard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher. You know three 1st-level wizard spells of your choice, two of which you must choose from the abjuration and evocation spells on the wizard spell list. The Spells Known column of the Eldritch Knight Spellcasting table shows when you learn more wizard spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be an abjuration or evocation spell of your choice, and must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level. The spells you learn at 8th, 14th, and 20th level can come from any school of magic.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your wizard spells, since you learn your spells through study and memorization. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a wizard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

features.name: Weapon Bond
description: At 3rd level, you learn a ritual that creates a magical bond between yourself and one weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest. The weapon must be within your reach throughout the ritual, at the conclusion of which you touch the weapon and forge the bond.

Once you have bonded a weapon to yourself, you can't be disarmed of that weapon unless you are incapacitated. If it is on the same plane of existence, you can summon that weapon as a bonus action on your turn, causing it to teleport instantly to your hand.
You can have up to two bonded weapons, but can summon only one at a time with your bonus action. If you attempt to bond with a third weapon, you must break the bond with one of the other two.

features.name: War Magic
description: Beginning at 7th level, when you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Eldritch Strike
description: At 10th level, you learn how to make your weapon strikes undercut a creature's resistance to your spells. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

features.name: Arcane Charge
description: At 15th level, you gain the ability to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see when you use your Action Surge. You can teleport before or after the additional action.

features.name: Improved War Magic
description: Starting at 18th level, when you use your action to cast a spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Samurai
description: The Samurai is a fighter who draws on an implacable fighting spirit to overcome enemies. A Samurai's resolve is nearly unbreakable, and the Samurai's fighting spirit grants strength and speed.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

choices.name: History
choices.description: Gain proficiency in History skill.

choices.name: Insight
choices.description: Gain proficiency in Insight skill.

choices.name: Performance
choices.description: Gain proficiency in Performance skill.

choices.name: Persuasion
choices.description: Gain proficiency in Persuasion skill.

choices.name: Language (choice)
choices.description: Learn one language of your choice.

features.name: Fighting Spirit
description: Starting at 3rd level, your intensity in battle can shield you and help you strike true. As a bonus action on your turn, you can give yourself advantage on weapon attack rolls until the end of your current turn, gaining 5 temporary hit points. The number of temporary hit points increases to 10 at 10th level and to 15 at 15th level. You can use this feature three times, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Elegant Courtier
description: Starting at 7th level, your discipline and attention to detail allow you to excel in social situations. Whenever you make a Wisdom (Insight) check, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10. In addition, you gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have proficiency in Wisdom saving throws, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (your choice).

features.name: Tireless Spirit
description: Starting at 10th level, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Fighting Spirit remaining, you regain one use.

features.name: Rapid Strike
description: Starting at 15th level, you can sacrifice accuracy to make additional strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can forgo advantage on one of the attacks to make an additional weapon attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Strength Before Death
description: Starting at 18th level, your fighting spirit can delay the grasp of death. If you take damage that reduces you to 0 hit points and doesn't kill you outright, you can use your reaction to delay falling unconscious, and you can immediately take an extra turn, interrupting the current turn. While you have 0 hit points during that extra turn, taking damage causes a death saving throw failure, and three failures can kill you. When the extra turn ends, you fall unconscious if you still have 0 hit points. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Four Elements
description: Monks of the Way of the Four Elements harness the power of the elements—earth, air, fire, and water—to perform fantastic feats. Through rigorous training and meditation, they learn to channel ki to create elemental effects.

These monks study the natural world and learn to emulate its forces. They can summon blasts of fire, create walls of stone, call down lightning, and even fly on the wind. Their training is both physically and mentally demanding.

features.name: Disciple of the Elements
description: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you learn magical disciplines that harness the power of the four elements. You know the Elemental Attunement discipline and one other elemental discipline of your choice. You learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice at 6th, 11th, and 17th level. Whenever you learn a new elemental discipline, you can also replace one elemental discipline that you already know with a different discipline.

Casting Elemental Spells. Some elemental disciplines allow you to cast spells. See chapter 10 for the general rules of spellcasting. To cast one of these spells, you use its casting time and other rules, but you don't need to provide material components. Once you reach 5th level in this class, you can spend additional ki points to increase the level of an elemental discipline spell that you cast, provided that the spell has an enhanced effect at a higher level, as Burning Hands does. Each additional ki point you spend increases the spell's level by 1. For example, if you are a 5th-level monk and use Fangs of the Fire Snake, you can spend 1 ki point to cast it as a 2nd-level spell.
Elemental Disciplines:

Elemental Attunement (L3). You can use your action to briefly control elemental forces within 30 feet of you, causing one of the following effects of your choice: Create a harmless, instantaneous sensory effect related to fire, water, air, or earth; Light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire; Chill or warm up to 1 pound of nonliving water by 10 degrees Fahrenheit; Cause earth, fire, or water that fits within a 1-foot cube to shape itself into a crude form you designate.

Fangs of the Fire Snake (L3). When you use the Attack action, you can spend 1 ki point to cause tendrils of flame to stretch out from your fists and feet. Your reach with your unarmed strikes increases by 10 feet for that action, and the damage of these strikes becomes fire damage instead of bludgeoning damage. If you spend 1 ki point when you hit with these attacks, the target also takes 1d10 fire damage.
Fist of the Four Thunders (L3). You can spend 2 ki points to cast thunderwave (1st level).

Fist of Unbroken Air (L3). You can spend 2 ki points to create a blast of compressed air that strikes like a fist. A creature within 30 feet must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage plus your Wisdom modifier, is pushed up to 20 feet away, and is knocked prone.
Ride the Wind (L3). You can spend 2 ki points to cast levitate (2nd level).
River of Hungry Flame (L3). You can spend 3 ki points to cast wall of fire (2nd level).
Clench of the North Wind (L6). You can spend 3 ki points to cast hold person (2nd level).
Gong of the Summit (L6). You can spend 3 ki points to cast shatter (2nd level).
Flames of the Phoenix (L11). You can spend 4 ki points to cast fireball (3rd level).
Mist Stance (L11). You can spend 4 ki points to cast gaseous form (3rd level).
Wave of Rolling Earth (L11). You can spend 4 ki points to cast wall of stone (3rd level).
Breath of Winter (L17). You can spend 6 ki points to cast cone of cold (5th level).
Eternal Mountain Defense (L17). You can spend 5 ki points to cast stoneskin (4th level).
River of Blood (L17). You can spend 6 ki points to cast cloudkill (5th level).

choices.description: Choose one elemental discipline (in addition to Elemental Attunement).

subclasses.name: Open Hand
description: Monks of the Way of the Open Hand are the ultimate masters of martial arts combat, whether armed or unarmed. They learn techniques to push and trip their opponents, manipulate ki to heal damage to their bodies, and practice advanced meditation that can protect them from harm.

features.name: Open Hand Technique
description:
Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate your enemy's ki when you harness your own. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target:
- It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
- It must make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, you can push it up to 15 feet away from you.
- It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Wholeness of Body
