41-42: A creature other than you within 30 feet of you is poisoned for 1d4 hours.
43-44: You cast Polymorph on yourself. If you fail the saving throw, you turn into a sheep for the duration.
45-46: For the next minute, any flammable object you touch that isn't being worn or carried bursts into flame.
47-48: You regain your lowest-level expended spell slot.
49-50: For the next minute, you must shout when you speak.
51-52: You cast Mirror Image on yourself.
53-54: You cast Fly on a random creature within 30 feet of you.
55-56: You become invisible for the next minute. During that time, other creatures can't hear you. The invisibility ends if you attack or cast a spell.
57-58: You cast Stinking Cloud centered on yourself.
59-60: Up to three creatures you choose within 30 feet of you take 4d10 fire damage.
61-62: You cast Speak with Dead.
63-64: You can immediately take one additional action.
65-66: You are teleported up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see.
67-68: The nearest door within 60 feet of you becomes a portal to a random plane for 1 minute.
69-70: A unicorn controlled by the DM appears in a space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later.
71-72: You are teleported to the Astral Plane until the end of your next turn, after which time you return to the space you previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space.
73-74: Maximize the damage of the next damaging spell you cast at a higher level.
75-76: Roll a d10. Your age changes by a number of years equal to the roll. If the roll is odd, you get younger (minimum 1 year). If the roll is even, you get older.
77-78: 1d6 flumphs controlled by the DM appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you and are frightened of you. They vanish after 1 minute.
79-80: You cast Polymorph on yourself. If you fail the saving throw, you turn into a sheep for the duration.
81-82: For the next minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a bonus action on each of your turns.
83-84: You cast Sunburst centered on yourself.
85-86: A mind flayer chosen and controlled by the DM appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later.
87-88: For the next minute, a random creature within 60 feet of you is poisoned.
89-90: You are immune to intoxication for the next 5d6 days.
91-92: Your hands become covered in sticky goo for the next minute.
93-94: You cast Greater Invisibility on yourself.
95-96: Your gender is changed for 1d10 days.
97-98: The next creature you hit with an attack takes an extra 1d6 force damage from the attack.
99-00: You regain all expended sorcery points.

features.name: Tides of Chaos
description: Starting at 1st level, you can manipulate the forces of chance and chaos to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

Any time before you regain the use of this feature, the DM can have you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher. You then regain the use of this feature.

features.name: Bend Luck
description: Starting at 6th level, you have the ability to twist fate using your wild magic. When another creature you can see makes an ability check or a saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll 4d4 and apply the number rolled as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the creature's ability check or saving throw.
You can do so after the creature rolls but before the outcome is determined.

features.name: Controlled Chaos
description: At 14th level, you gain a modicum of control over the surges of your wild magic. Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, you can roll twice and use either number.

features.name: Spell Bombardment
description: At 18th level, the power of your spells is amplified by the magic of chaos. When you roll damage for a spell and roll the same number on two or more of the dice, you can reroll one of the dice. You must use the new roll, and you can only use this feature once per turn.

subclasses.name: Archfey
description: Your patron is a lord or lady of the fey, a creature of legend who holds secrets that were forgotten before the mortal races were born. These beings are capricious and unpredictable, but they can grant great power to those who serve them.

The Archfey patron represents the wild magic of the fey courts. Warlocks who serve these beings gain abilities that reflect the fey's connection to nature and illusion, including the power to charm and beguile others.

features.name: Fey Presence
features.description: Starting at 1st level, your patron bestows upon you the ability to project the beguiling and fearsome presence of the fey. As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. The creatures that fail their saving throws are all charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Misty Escape
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can vanish in a puff of mist in response to harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
features.description: Beginning at 10th level, your patron teaches you how to turn the mind-affecting magic of your enemies against them. You are immune to being charmed, and when another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to attempt to turn the charm back on that creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.

features.name: Dark Delirium
features.description: Starting at 14th level, you can plunge a creature into an illusory realm. As an action, choose a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute or until your concentration is broken (as if you are concentrating on a spell). This effect ends early if the creature takes any damage. Until this illusion ends, the creature thinks it is lost in a misty realm, the appearance of which you choose. The creature can see and hear only itself, you, and the illusion. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this feature again.

subclasses.name: Fiend
description: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. Such beings desire the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you. Fiends powerful enough to forge a pact include demon lords such as Demogorgon, Orcus, Fraz'Urb-luu, and Baphomet; archdevils such as Asmodeus, Dispater, Mephistopheles, and Belial; pit fiends and balors that are especially mighty; and ultroloths and other lords of the yugoloths.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
description: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
description:
Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
description: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
description:
Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape.
At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Great Old One
description: Your patron is a being from beyond the stars, an entity of immense power and alien intelligence. The Great Old One might be a sleeping god, an ancient aberration, or a being from another plane of existence entirely.

Those who make pacts with such beings often find their minds expanded, gaining access to telepathic abilities and forbidden knowledge. However, the price of such power can be high, as the Great Old One's influence can slowly drive mortals to madness.

features.name: Awakened Mind
description: At 1st level, you can communicate telepathically.

features.name: Entropic Ward
description: At 6th level, you can impose disadvantage on an attack roll against you.

features.name: Thought Shield
description: At 10th level, you have resistance to psychic damage.

features.name: Create Thrall
description: At 14th level, you can charm a creature.

subclasses.name: Hexblade
description: You have made a pact with a mysterious entity from the Shadowfell—a force that manifests in sentient magic weapons. The Hexblade might have forged the blade you wield as your pact weapon, or it might have revealed itself through a ritual of dark binding.

The Hexblade patron represents the power of the Shadowfell and its connection to death and darkness. Warlocks who serve these beings gain abilities that reflect this connection, including the power to curse their enemies and channel dark energy through their weapons.

features.name: Hexblade's Curse
features.description: Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to place a bitter curse on someone. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target is cursed for 1 minute. The curse ends early if the target dies, you die, or you are incapacitated. Until the curse ends, you gain the following benefits: You gain a bonus to damage rolls against the cursed target. The bonus equals your proficiency bonus. Any attack roll you make against the cursed target is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. If the target dies, you regain hit points equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Hex Warrior
features.description: At 1st level, you acquire the training necessary to effectively arm yourself for battle. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons. The influence of your patron also allows you to mystically channel your will through a particular weapon. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one weapon that you are proficient with and that lacks the two-handed property. When you attack with that weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls. This benefit lasts until you finish a long rest again. If you later gain the Pact of the Blade feature, this benefit applies to any pact weapon you conjure with that feature, no matter the weapon's type.

features.name: Accursed Specter
features.description: Starting at 6th level, you can curse the soul of a slain enemy and bind it to your service. When you slay a humanoid, you can cause its spirit to rise as a specter. When the specter appears, it gains temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level. Roll initiative for the specter, which has its own turns. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you), and it gains a special bonus to its attack rolls equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +0). The specter remains in your service until the end of your next long rest, at which point it vanishes to the afterlife. Once you bind a specter with this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Armor of Hexes
features.description: At 10th level, your hex grows more powerful. If the target cursed by your Hexblade's Curse hits you with an attack, roll a d6. On a roll of 4 or higher, the attack instead misses you, regardless of its roll. This ability functions against attack rolls made by both creatures and objects.

features.name: Master of Hexes
features.description: Starting at 14th level, the curse you place on a foe spreads to another when its host falls. When the humanoid you have cursed is reduced to 0 hit points and dies, you can apply the curse to a different humanoid you can see within 30 feet of you. When you transfer the curse, you don't regain uses of the Hexblade's Curse feature.

subclasses.name: The Celestial
description: A Celestial patron is a being of the Upper Planes. A celestial warlock is a champion of the forces of good and light, and they channel the power of their patron to heal and protect.

features.name: Bonus Cantrips
description: When you choose this patron at 1st level, you learn the sacred flame and light cantrips. They count as warlock cantrips for you, but they don't count against your number of cantrips known.

features.name: Healing Light
description: At 1st level, you gain a pool of magical energy represented by a number of d6s equal to 1 + your warlock level. As a bonus action, you can heal one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The maximum number of dice you can spend on a turn equals your Charisma modifier (minimum of one die). Roll the spent dice and add them together. The target regains a number of hit points equal to the total. You regain all expended dice when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Radiant Soul
description: Starting at 6th level, your connection to the Celestial allows you to serve as a conduit for radiant energy. You have resistance to radiant damage. Whenever you cast a spell that deals radiant or fire damage, you add your Charisma modifier to one radiant or fire damage roll of that spell against one of its targets.

features.name: Celestial Resilience
description: Starting at 10th level, you can draw on the resilience of the Celestial to protect yourself and your allies. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage type until the end of the current turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Searing Vengeance
description: At 14th level, the radiant energy you channel allows you to overcome death's grasp. When you are reduced to 0 hit points and aren't killed outright, you can use your reaction to instead drop to 1 hit point and shed bright light in a 30-foot radius. Each of your foes within that radius takes 2d8 + your Charisma modifier radiant damage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: The Fathomless
description: You have made a pact with an entity of the deep sea. A fathomless warlock is a champion of the dark depths, and they channel the power of their patron to control the waters and the creatures that dwell within them.

features.name: Bonus Spells
description:
At 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Fathomless Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.

1st: create or destroy water, thunderwave
3rd: gust of wind, silence
5th: lightning bolt, sleet storm
7th: control water, summon elemental
9th: Bigby's hand, cone of cold
11th: conjure elemental, maelstrom

features.name: Tentacle of the Deep
description: At 1st level, you can summon a spectral tentacle that strikes at your foes. As a bonus action, you can create a 10-foot-long tentacle at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The tentacle lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature to create another tentacle. When you create the tentacle, you can make a melee spell attack against one creature within 10 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 cold damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. The tentacle can attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. The damage increases to 2d8 at 5th level, 3d8 at 11th level, and 4d8 at 17th level.

features.name: Gift of the Sea
description: At 6th level, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet, and you can breathe underwater.

features.name: Oceanic Soul
description: At 10th level, you gain resistance to cold damage. In addition, while you are fully submerged in water, you can communicate simple ideas with any beast that has an innate swimming speed.

features.name: Guardian Coil
description: At 14th level, your tentacle can defend you and your allies. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to choose one of the creatures and reduce the damage by 1d8. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can make a melee spell attack against the attacker as part of the same reaction. On a hit, the attacker takes 1d8 + your Charisma modifier cold damage.

features.name: Grasping Tentacles
description: At 18th level, you can call forth a manifestation of the deep. You can cast the evard's black tentacles spell, requiring no spell slot or material components. When you cast the spell in this way, the area of the spell is difficult terrain for creatures other than you. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: The Genie
description: You have made a pact with one of the genies, the mighty elemental rulers of the Inner Planes. A genie patron is a powerful being that can grant wishes and bend reality to its will.

features.name: Bonus Spells
description:
At 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Genie Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.

1st: detect evil and good, protection from evil and good
3rd: create food and water, phantasmal killer
5th: creation, sending
7th: creation, summon elemental
9th: creation, wall of stone
11th: creation, wish

features.name: Genie's Vessel
description:
At 1st level, your patron gifts you a magical vessel that grants you a measure of the genie's power. The vessel is a Tiny object, and you choose the object's nature: an oil lamp, an ornate urn, a gilded chalice, or some other similarly shaped Tiny object. While you are touching the vessel, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells. The vessel's AC equals your spell save DC. It has a number of hit points equal to your warlock level + your proficiency bonus, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage.

The vessel grants you the following benefits:

Elemental Gift: You gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.

Limited Wish: Once per long rest, you can cast a spell of 6th level or lower from the warlock spell list, requiring no spell slot or material components.

features.name: Elemental Gift
description: Starting at 6th level, the vessel grants you resistance to a damage type based on your patron's kind: fire (Dao), cold (Djinni), lightning (Efreeti), or thunder (Marid). You also gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.

features.name: Sanctuary Vessel
description: At 10th level, when you or an ally within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to whisk the damaged creature into your vessel. The creature is transported to the vessel's extradimensional space, where it is safe from harm. The creature remains there until the end of your next turn or until you use this feature again. When the creature reappears, it appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Limited Wish
description: At 14th level, you can tap into the power of your genie patron to cast powerful spells. Once per long rest, you can cast a spell of 6th level or lower from the warlock spell list, requiring no spell slot or material components.

subclasses.name: Undying
description: Your patron is a powerful undead being, such as a lich, vampire, or mummy lord. These beings have cheated death and gained immortality through dark magic, and they share some of their power with their warlock servants.

The Undying patron represents those who have transcended death, and its warlocks gain abilities that reflect this connection to undeath. They can resist disease, recover from wounds, and even cheat death itself.

features.name: Among the Dead
description: At 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

features.name: Undying Nature
description: Also at 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against disease.

features.name: Beyond the Grave
description: At 6th level, you can gain temporary hit points when you finish a short rest.

features.name: Indestructible Life
description: At 10th level, you can regain hit points when you take damage.

features.name: Undying Nature
description: At 14th level, you can't be killed by a single attack.

subclasses.name: Abjuration
description: The abjuration specialist is a wizard who focuses on protective and defensive magic. They are masters of wards, shields, and counterspells, able to protect themselves and their allies from magical and physical harm.

Abjurers study the theory and practice of defensive magic, learning to create magical barriers that can absorb damage and deflect attacks. They are often found on the front lines, using their abilities to keep their companions safe.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Arcane Ward
description: Also at 2nd level, you can create a magical ward.

features.name: Projected Ward
description: At 6th level, you can use your Arcane Ward to protect others.

features.name: Improved Abjuration
description: At 10th level, your Arcane Ward regains hit points when you finish a short rest.

features.name: Spell Resistance
description: At 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells.

subclasses.name: Bladesinging
description: Bladesingers are elves who have learned to combine swordplay with arcane magic. They are deadly warriors who use their magic to enhance their combat prowess.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this tradition at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with light armor, a one-handed melee weapon of your choice, and the Performance skill if you don't already have it.

features.name: Training in War and Song
description: Starting at 2nd level, you learn to blend your magic with your weapon work. You gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, History, or Performance. You also gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.

features.name: Bladesong
description:
Starting at 2nd level, you can invoke a secret elven magic called the Bladesong, provided you aren't wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield. It graces you with supernatural speed, agility, and focus. You can use a bonus action to start the Bladesong, which lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are incapacitated, if you don medium or heavy armor or a shield, or if you use two hands to make an attack with a weapon. You can also dismiss the Bladesong at any time you choose (no action required). While your Bladesong is active, you gain the following benefits:

You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

You have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.

You gain a bonus to any Constitution saving throw you make to maintain your concentration on a spell. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Extra Attack
description: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.

features.name: Song of Defense
description: At 10th level, you can direct your magic to absorb damage while your Bladesong is active. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to expend one spell slot and reduce that damage to you by an amount equal to five times the spell slot's level.

features.name: Song of Victory
description: At 14th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Bladesong is active.

subclasses.name: Chronurgy Magic
description: Chronurgy is the study of time magic. Chronurgists learn to manipulate the flow of time, slowing it down, speeding it up, or even reversing it.

features.name: Chronal Shift
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can magically exert limited control over the flow of time around a creature. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll a d8 and apply it to the roll. You can choose to use this feature after the roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw succeeds or fails. The d8 roll is added to the total if the roll is for an attack roll or ability check, or subtracted from the total if the roll is for a saving throw. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Temporal Awareness
description: Starting at 2nd level, you gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier. In addition, you can't be surprised while you are conscious.

features.name: Momentary Stasis
description: Starting at 6th level, you can use your command over time to force a creature to slow down. As an action, you can choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is restrained and incapacitated until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Arcane Abeyance
description: At 10th level, you can store a spell in a tiny, bead-like object. As an action, you can cast a spell of 4th level or lower into the bead, which holds the spell until it is used. The bead is a Tiny object, and it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to all damage except force damage. The bead is destroyed when the spell is cast or when you die. You can have only one bead at a time, and you can't create another until the spell in the bead is cast. The bead can be used by anyone who holds it. To use the spell, the creature holding the bead must use its action to cast the spell, using your spell save DC and spell attack bonus.

features.name: Convergent Future
description: Starting at 14th level, you can peer into the future and see the outcome of a course of action. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to ignore the roll. Instead, you can choose the result of the roll to be the highest or lowest possible. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Conjuration
description: Conjurers specialize in creating objects and creatures from nothing. They can summon weapons, armor, and even living creatures to aid them in battle or perform tasks.

The study of conjuration requires precision and spatial awareness. Conjurers learn to open portals to other planes, calling forth creatures and objects to serve their needs. They are versatile spellcasters who can adapt to any situation.

features.name: Conjuration Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Conjuration
description: Also at 2nd level, you can conjure small objects.

features.name: Benign Transportation
description: At 6th level, you can swap places with a creature.

features.name: Focused Conjuration
description: At 10th level, your concentration on conjuration spells is not broken when you take damage.

features.name: Durable Summons
description: At 14th level, your summoned creatures gain temporary hit points.

subclasses.name: Divination
description: Diviners study the art of predicting the future. They can glimpse moments yet to come, gaining insight into the outcomes of actions and the intentions of others.

The study of divination requires keen intellect and intuition. Diviners learn to read the signs and portents that others miss, using their knowledge to guide their allies and outmaneuver their enemies.

features.name: Divination Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Portent
description: Also at 2nd level, you can replace any attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

features.name: Expert Divination
description: At 6th level, you can regain spell slots when you cast divination spells.

features.name: Third Eye
description: At 10th level, you can gain darkvision, see invisible creatures, etc.

features.name: Greater Portent
description: At 14th level, you can cast the foresight spell once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Enchantment
description: Enchanters specialize in manipulating the minds of others. They can charm, beguile, and control creatures, turning enemies into allies and bending others to their will.

The study of enchantment requires subtlety and finesse. Enchanters learn to weave spells that influence thoughts and emotions, using their abilities to avoid conflict or gain advantage in social situations.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Hypnotic Gaze
description: Also at 2nd level, you can charm a creature with a look.

features.name: Instinctive Charm
description: At 6th level, you can divert attacks made against you.

features.name: Split Enchantment
description: At 10th level, you can target two creatures with enchantment spells.

features.name: Alter Memories
description: At 14th level, you can modify a creature's memory.

subclasses.name: Evocation
description: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar. Others use their spectacular power to protect the weak, while some seek their own gain as bandits, adventurers, or aspiring tyrants.

features.name: Evocation Savant
description: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
description: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
description: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
description: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
description:
Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

subclasses.name: Graviturgy Magic
description: Graviturgy is the study of gravity magic. Graviturgists learn to manipulate the force of gravity, making themselves and their allies lighter or heavier, and even creating gravitational anomalies.

features.name: Adjust Density
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your command of gravity to alter the weight of a creature. As an action, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature's weight is halved or doubled (your choice) for 1 minute. While the creature's weight is halved, its walking speed increases by 10 feet, and it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. While the creature's weight is doubled, its walking speed decreases by 10 feet, and it has disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Gravity Well
description: Starting at 6th level, you can create a point of intense gravitational force. When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can choose one creature that fails its saving throw. That creature is pulled 10 feet toward you, provided you can see it and it is within 60 feet of you.

features.name: Violent Attraction
description: Starting at 10th level, you can use your command of gravity to increase the force of your attacks. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can use a bonus action to choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature takes force damage equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you can move it 10 feet toward you or away from you (your choice). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Gravity Sinkhole
description: At 14th level, you can create a devastating gravitational anomaly. As an action, you can choose a point you can see within 120 feet of you. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 force damage and is restrained until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't restrained. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Illusion
description: Illusionists create false images and manipulate perceptions. They can make things appear or disappear, create phantasmal creatures, and alter the appearance of themselves and others.
The study of illusion requires creativity and imagination. Illusionists learn to bend light and sound, creating realistic illusions that can deceive even the most perceptive observers.

features.name: Illusion Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an illusion spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Improved Minor Illusion
description: Also at 2nd level, you can change the nature of your illusions.

features.name: Illusory Self
description: At 6th level, you can create an illusory duplicate of yourself.

features.name: Illusory Self
description: At 10th level, you can make an illusion real.

features.name: Illusory Reality
description: At 14th level, you can create an illusory creature.

subclasses.name: Necromancy
description: Necromancers study the forces of life and death. They can animate the dead, drain life force from living creatures, and even cheat death itself.

The study of necromancy requires a strong will and a willingness to confront the darker aspects of existence. Necromancers learn to harness the power of negative energy, using it to create undead servants and protect themselves from harm.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a necromancy spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Grim Harvest
description: Also at 2nd level, you can regain hit points when you kill a creature.

features.name: Undead Thralls
description: At 6th level, you can animate undead.

features.name: Inured to Undeath
description: At 10th level, you have resistance to necrotic damage.

features.name: Command Undead
description: At 14th level, you can command undead creatures.

subclasses.name: Order of Scribes
description: The Order of Scribes is a tradition of wizards who believe that magic is a language. They study the written word and the arcane symbols that make up spells, and they use their knowledge to create new spells and modify existing ones.

features.name: Wizardly Quill
description: At 2nd level, you can use a special quill to write spells into your spellbook. The quill doesn't require ink. When you use the quill to copy a spell into your spellbook, you can reduce the time and cost to copy the spell by half. You can also use the quill to create a spell scroll. When you do so, you must provide the spell's components, and the scroll costs half the normal amount of gold to create.

features.name: Awakened Spellbook
description:
Starting at 2nd level, you have a spellbook that has been awakened by your magic. The spellbook has the following benefits:

You can use the spellbook as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells.

When you cast a wizard spell with a spell slot, you can temporarily replace its damage type with the damage type of another spell in your spellbook of the same level. This replacement lasts for the duration of the spell.

When you cast a wizard spell as a ritual, you can use the spell's normal casting time, rather than adding 10 minutes to it. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

If your spellbook is lost, you can perform a special ritual to create a new one. This ritual takes 8 hours to complete, and you must have access to a wizard's spellbook to copy spells from. The new spellbook becomes your awakened spellbook.

features.name: Manifest Mind
description: Starting at 6th level, you can cause your spellbook to manifest a spectral mind. As a bonus action, you can cause the mind to appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of you. The mind is a Tiny object, and it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to all damage except force damage. The mind is invisible, and it can't be targeted by attacks or spells. The mind lasts for 1 hour, until you dismiss it as a bonus action, or until you die. While the mind is present, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells. In addition, you can cast spells as if you were in the mind's space, provided you can see the mind.

features.name: Master Scrivian
description: Starting at 10th level, you can create powerful scrolls. When you finish a long rest, you can create a number of spell scrolls equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one). The scrolls must be for spells of 5th level or lower, and the spells must be in your spellbook. The scrolls cost half the normal amount of gold to create, and they last for 8 hours before becoming inert.

features.name: One with Words
description: At 14th level, your mastery of the written word allows you to cast spells without speaking. When you cast a wizard spell, you can cast it without verbal components. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Transmutation
description: Transmuters manipulate the physical world. They can change the shape and properties of objects, transform one substance into another, and even alter their own bodies.

The study of transmutation requires a deep understanding of the natural world. Transmuters learn to reshape reality at a fundamental level, using their abilities to adapt to any situation and overcome any obstacle.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a transmutation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Alchemy
description: Also at 2nd level, you can transmute materials.

features.name: Transmuter's Stone
description: At 6th level, you can create a stone that grants benefits.

features.name: Shapechanger
description: At 10th level, you can cast the polymorph spell on yourself.

features.name: Master Transmuter
description: At 14th level, you can transmute matter at a touch.

subclasses.name: War Magic
description: The War Magic tradition is a school of wizardry that focuses on the practical application of magic in combat. War mages are skilled in both offensive and defensive magic, and they use their knowledge to survive on the battlefield.

features.name: Arcane Deflection
description: At 2nd level, you learn to weave your magic into a protective shield. When you are hit by an attack or you fail a saving throw against a spell or other magical effect, you can use your reaction to gain a +2 bonus to your AC against that attack or a +4 bonus to that saving throw. If you do so, you can't cast spells other than cantrips until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Tactical Wit
description: Starting at 2nd level, you add your Intelligence modifier to your initiative rolls.

features.name: Power Surge
description: Starting at 6th level, you can store magical energy inside your body to fuel your spells. You have a pool of power surges, represented by a number of d6s equal to your wizard level. When you make an attack roll or a saving throw, you can spend one power surge to add the roll of one d6 to the total. You can use this feature only once per turn. You regain all expended power surges when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Durable Magic
description: At 10th level, the spells you cast help sustain your defenses. While you are maintaining concentration on a spell, you gain a +2 bonus to AC and to all saving throws.

features.name: Deflecting Shroud
description: At 14th level, your Arcane Deflection becomes more powerful. When you use your Arcane Deflection, you can choose up to three creatures within 10 feet of you. The bonus you gain from Arcane Deflection is granted to those creatures as well.
